entries.headline: The building for Denmark’s quantum computer is finished. The computer is not.
entries.dek: MAGNE’s Copenhagen facility cleared handover on 2 September; installation is only now beginning and full operation is expected in spring 2027. That makes a 2025 delivery promise measurable — and we just measured it.

source.name: The Quantum Insider
source.title: QuNorth Clears Facility Milestone for MAGNE Quantum Computer, 2 September 2026

entries.headline: Xanadu put a date on 1,000 logical qubits — and published the number it has to fix first
entries.dek: More than 1,000 logical qubits by 2031, fault tolerance in 2028–2029, a quantum data centre by 2030. Also: a photon-loss figure that has to fall from 24.1× to 1.0×. The second number is the honest one.

source.name: The Quantum Insider
source.title: Xanadu Targets More Than 1,000 Logical Qubits by 2031, 31 August 2026 (reporting Xanadu's published roadmap)

entries.headline: A “quantum-safe” satellite link went live over Doha — and the word is doing two different jobs
entries.dek: Arqit, Es’hailSat and AIEE ran quantum-safe key agreement across an operating satellite link with no hardware swap. Worth being precise about what was, and was not, quantum about it.

source.name: Arqit Quantum Inc.
source.title: Arqit, Es'hailSat and AIEE Demonstrate Quantum-Safe Satellite Security, press release, 1 September 2026

entries.headline: Fujitsu has a diamond-spin quantum computer working — and has not said how big it is
entries.dek: Tin-vacancy centres built into photonic integrated circuits, running at −271.6 °C. The temperature is the interesting number. The missing qubit count is the interesting silence.

source.name: The Quantum Insider
source.title: Fujitsu develops diamond-spin quantum computer prototype, 8 September 2026 (reporting Fujitsu's own announcement)

entries.headline: IBM and Chicago ran 70 logical qubits — and could prove the answer was right
entries.dek: 2,415 logical two-qubit gates and 468 T gates, at effective error rates about ten times below the physical ones underneath. The new part is not the size. It is that the result is checkable.

source.name: arXiv
source.title: Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity (arXiv:2607.25941); reported by The Quantum Insider, 31 July 2026
